page: Microsoft Azure D32pls_v6 is an ARM64-based virtual machine powered by a dedicated Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor. Operating at 3.4 GHz, it features 32 physical cores and 32 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core ratio, meaning hyperthreading is disabled. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It is configured with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark testing, the D32pls_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, highlighted by a strong stress-ng multi-core score of 66293.46 and a strong multi-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 339.37 GB/sec. Memory performance is particularly notable, with top-tier results in uncached large-block read and write bandwidth, alongside a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database operations also rank in the top tier, scoring 38223.2. However, single-core performance remains average, as seen in stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core metrics. Large LLM inference workloads show limitations, with prompt processing speeds falling into the bottom 10% tier.

The low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core positions this instance as a cost-efficient option for compute-intensive tasks that do not demand massive memory footprints. It is well-suited for multi-threaded workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and database operations that benefit from high memory bandwidth and dedicated physical cores. Conversely, it is less suitable for memory-intensive databases or large-scale AI model inference.
